title: Measure AI quality before changing it
outcome: Report quality and escalation rates without hiding failures.
story: A new prompt answers more messages, but Amina suspects it makes more wrong promises. Measure correctness and coverage together before deciding that it is better.

frames.explanation: Answer precision improves, while coverage falls. Both changes matter.
An average score can hide a dangerous incorrect refund or policy promise.

sections.title: Create a labelled dataset
paragraphs: An evaluation dataset contains representative inputs and agreed expected outcomes. Include normal, ambiguous, malformed, missing-source, cross-shop, and adversarial cases. Keep input, label, reason, and source evidence together.

Separate a development set used for tuning from a held-out set used for comparison. Repeatedly changing a prompt after reading every held-out failure turns that set into development data. Collect new cases and document how labels were reviewed.

sections.title: Measure several outcomes
paragraphs: Accuracy measures all exactly correct outcomes, including a correct human fallback. Coverage measures the fraction answered without human fallback. Answer precision measures correct automated answers divided by all automated answers.

An assistant that always says human can have zero coverage. An assistant that answers everything can have poor precision. Decide an acceptable tradeoff using the costs of false answers and review workload; do not choose the highest-looking number alone.

sections.title: Review failures, not only averages
paragraphs: Record each failure’s category and severity. A wrong promise involving money may require a release stop even if the average accuracy is high. Treat permission violations and secret exposure as failures independently of language quality.

Keep prompt, model, schema, retrieval index, and dataset versions. Save latency, actual usage, refusals, and timeouts. Fixture tests prove deterministic control behaviour; real-model runs supply separate quality evidence.

sections.title: Make changes comparable
paragraphs: Run old and new versions on the same labelled inputs and inspect the changed outcomes. Repeat real runs when randomness or provider behaviour matters. Note sample size and variability rather than claiming certainty from a tiny set.

Add each reproduced incident as a regression case. Keep the regression focused on the failure while still running the broader suite. Require human review of important release decisions instead of equating one aggregate threshold with safety.

exercise.title: An honest evaluation report
exercise.brief: Write score(rows), where each row has expected and actual. actual=human counts as escalation. Return total, correct, accuracy, coverage, answerPrecision; use zero for any empty denominator.

steps.title: Count exact matches
steps.task: Return only total and correct for this step.
steps.hint: Filter rows whose actual equals expected.

steps.title: Add accuracy
steps.task: Add accuracy = correct / total, or zero when empty. Earlier output shapes now include accuracy.

steps.title: Add coverage and answer precision
steps.task: Return the final five fields. Count answered rows separately from all correct rows.
steps.hint: A correct human fallback affects accuracy but not answer precision.

project.title: An evaluation-driven change
project.brief: Prepare a dataset, compare two assistant versions, and write a release recommendation that includes the worst failures.
deliverables: A reviewed development and held-out dataset.
A version comparison and release recommendation.

milestones.title: Run both versions
actions: Record quality, coverage, latency, and usage.

milestones.title: Decide from evidence
actions: Add a reproduced incident as a regression.
Recommend release, revision, or further evidence.

acceptance: The held-out set stays separate from tuning.
Coverage and precision are both reported.
The report identifies every version and execution mode.

tests.situation: New version invents one costly promise
tests.expected: The failure is visible despite a good average.
The report does not claim validated quality.
